q: The gaseous state is the _____ state of matter to understand.
e: The gaseous state is the simplest state of matter to understand. The gaseous state is the simplest to understand because particles are far apart and attractions are weak. Among the three states, the gas model is the easiest because particles are far apart with weak forces. Simplest is the word this version is asking about.

q: _____ gas is required to keep our bodies alive.
e: Oxygen gas is required to keep our bodies alive. Cells use oxygen in respiration to stay alive, so that is the gas the body cannot do without. nitrogen is plentiful in air but does not keep cells alive. Oxygen is the word this version is asking about.

q: Carbon dioxide is a gas given off as waste by animals and used as a raw material by _____.
e: Carbon dioxide is a gas given off as waste by animals and used as a raw material by plants. Animals give off carbon dioxide, and plants take that gas as a raw material for photosynthesis. Plants is the word this version is asking about.
Methane gas is used as fuel. Methane is the hydrocarbon gas burned as a fuel. Methane is the word this version is asking about.

q: Ammonia gas is a combination of nitrogen and _____ gases.
e: Ammonia gas is a combination of nitrogen and hydrogen gases. Ammonia is NH3, a combination of nitrogen with hydrogen.

q: Ammonia gas is used to make _____.
e: Ammonia gas is used to make fertiliser. Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen and is the feedstock for nitrogen fertiliser.

q: The volume and shape of all gases can be assumed as those of their _____.
e: The volume and shape of all gases can be assumed as those of their containers. A gas has no shape or volume of its own, so it takes the shape and volume of its container. Containers is the word this version is asking about.

q: The intermolecular forces of gases are much _____ than those of other physical states.
e: The intermolecular forces of gases are much weaker than those of other physical states. Intermolecular forces in a gas are weak because the particles sit far apart compared with a liquid or solid. That comparison is with those of other physical states.

q: Being the most _____ of the states of matter, gases can be mixed evenly and completely.
e: Being the most compressible of the states of matter, gases can be mixed evenly and completely. Gases are the most compressible state because most of the volume is empty space between particles.

q: Gases have much _____ densities than liquids and solids.
e: Gases have much lower densities than liquids and solids. Gas density is low because a small mass is spread through a large empty volume. That comparison is with liquids and solids.

q: The Kinetic Molecular Theory is a model that is used to predict _____.
e: The Kinetic Molecular Theory is a model that is used to predict gas behaviour. The kinetic molecular theory treats a gas as tiny particles in constant random motion with lots of empty space between them. Gas behaviour is the word this version is asking about.

q: The volume of the particles themselves is _____ compared with the total volume of the gas.
e: The volume of the particles themselves is negligible compared with the total volume of the gas. The particles' own volume is negligible next to the volume of the gas, which is mostly empty space. Negligible is the word this version is asking about.

q: Most of the volume of the gas is _____.
e: Most of the volume of the gas is empty space. Most of a gas's volume is empty space, so the particles themselves take up a negligible share. Empty space is the word this version is asking about.

q: Gas molecules are in constant motion in _____ directions.
e: Gas molecules are in constant motion in random directions. Gas particles travel in random straight-line bursts and change direction only when they collide.

Collisions among molecules are perfectly elastic. Elastic collisions keep the total kinetic energy of the particles. energy is not lost as heat in the ideal-gas picture. Elastic is the word this version is asking about.

q: The total energy of all the molecules in a system remains the _____.
e: The total energy of all the molecules in a system remains the same. Ideal-gas collisions are elastic, so the total kinetic energy of the molecules stays the same. Same is the word this version is asking about.

q: Gas molecules exert neither attractive nor _____ forces on one another.
e: Gas molecules exert neither attractive nor repulsive forces on one another. Ideal gas particles are treated as having no attractions or repulsions, only collisions. Repulsive is the word this version is asking about.

q: The average kinetic energy of molecules is the same for all gases at the same _____.
e: The average kinetic energy of molecules is the same for all gases at the same temperature. Kelvin temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the gas particles. Temperature is the word this version is asking about.

q: The average kinetic energy is directly proportional to the _____ temperature.
e: The average kinetic energy is directly proportional to the Kelvin temperature. Kelvin temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the gas particles. Gas laws use Kelvin because that scale starts at absolute zero, where particle motion would stop.
